$comment: The class of every string field of every client request, client notification and answer to a server request, with its reason: `free` (a lone surrogate there is read as U+FFFD) or `refused` (a lone surrogate there refuses the frame). It is the independent statement src/free_text.rs FREE_TEXT must equal: the contract test (tests/it/contract.rs every_string_field_is_classed_once_and_free_text_is_listed_free) fails on a field of the schema in no class or in two, a classed field the schema does not have, and any difference between the `free` fields here and FREE_TEXT, either way. Fields are pointers into the payload; `*` is any one array index or map key, a last `{}` the keys of the map there, a last `**` every value and key below. `payloads` enumerates, for each value the schema leaves untyped, the string fields its reader reads (`fields`, or the `schema` definition it deserialises into), with that reader as `source`; `open` names a part that has no fixed fields by nature (JSON a model, a tool, a provider or the language-server protocol wrote, or a setting value whose shape its path decides) with its class and reason: only such a part may be classed whole as `**`.

/params/diagnostics/*/data.reason: a code action's diagnostics' server data, sent back for the server to match its own diagnostic: refused whole

/event/value.source: native/core/crates/mixdog-core-domains/src/domains/ai_admin/model_proxy.rs event_in (citations, server tool blocks, thinking blocks)

open.reason: text a model or a web page wrote (citations, thinking)
a provider's raw usage object, kept as given

classes.reason: A Goal's objective, typed or as a `/goal` command.

A model call run on the desktop: the conversation's text, a model's output, a tool's description and schema, a provider's error text; forwarded to and from the provider, never compared (model and tool names, ids and provider state stay refused).
A patch's text (file content), given to `git apply`.
A person's answer to a tool approval or a question (the decision itself is `approved`/`response`, an enum).
A server's arguments and environment values as a person typed them (the names stay identifiers): given to the server's process as Node's spawn gave them (U+FFFD).
A skill's name is checked to `[a-z0-9-]` (mixdog-mcp skills.rs `validate_name`): one that held a lone unit is refused by that check with Node's message, as Node's was.
Commit messages, given to git as Node's spawn gave them (U+FFFD).

File content being written: the workspace refuses it with Node's message (mixdog-workspace fsops.rs `check_paired`); a document's text as an editor holds it. A save's expected content is file text too: the workspace marks one that held a lone unit, and it equals no file Node would have saved over (a lossless file never holds one): refused at Node's comparison with Node's sentence (mixdog-workspace fsops.rs `expected_text`; recorded, native/core/fixtures/inbound-lone-surrogate).

Search queries: a plain-text workspace one matches nothing, as Node's matched nothing (mixdog-workspace textsearch.rs, search.rs); the others search for U+FFFD, the documented difference (decisions.md); git gets what Node's spawn gave it.
Text stored as written: notes, personas, definitions, instructions, prompts, descriptions.
Text typed into a remote browser page or a terminal, written to the page or the pty as UTF-8 (Node's write gave the unit as U+FFFD too); a log line.
The text of a turn, a steer or a queued message (the steer and the queue send turn/start's input), a `/goal` command typed in the composer, the composer's text handed back with a queued entry.
Titles, names and renames shown as typed (the record's id is separate).

Values a person types into a form. A workflow's inputs: a JSON body. A custom provider's extra body fields: a JSON body, whose size the core measures as Node's JSON.stringify does, each lone unit as its six-character escape (mixdog-core-domains ai_account/custom_config.rs normalize_request_body). A custom provider's header values: Node's check refuses a value outside Latin-1 with `[custom-provider] headers.<name> has an invalid value`, and the core's check refuses U+FFFD with the same text before anything is sent (normalize_headers). A probed MCP server's header values: never sent, any header is configured authentication, Node and the core answer {auth: configured}. Recorded: native/core/fixtures/lone-surrogate-wire (custom-*-header-lone, custom-*-body-*, mcp-probe-header-lone).
What a page or a model shows: visualize tab labels, titles and inline content, a page's title and error.
What the desktop publishes as text: a web page's title (a page may set one holding a lone unit), an import's or the updater's error message, a monitor's name.
a URL, host, domain, port or transport, parsed and matched
a close reason code the phone's WebRTC stack writes
a duration, parsed into a number of milliseconds; text holding a lone unit is no duration and Node refused it in the same parser

a file's name: compared with a folder's entries before a file is made or opened, or the name of a file the client read from disk; a name holding a lone unit names no file Node would have found (decisions.md "frame-lone-surrogate")
a git ref, commit, tag or config key, or a worktree name that becomes a branch and folder name: matched against the repository; git and Node's ref checks refuse a ref that is not well-formed text
a git ref, commit, tag or label: matched against the repository, whose ref checks refuse a ref that is not well-formed text
a kind, mode, scope, phase, sort, state or other word from a fixed vocabulary the reader matches, written by the client app, never typed text

a map's key: an id, a name or a parameter the reader looks the value up by (an environment variable, a header, an attachment or a model parameter); a key is never typed text, and two keys that read as one would overwrite each other
a model, provider, route, effort, tool, connector, plugin, workflow or agent id from a catalog, matched against it
a path, or a file, command or record name compared with what is on disk or in a store: a name holding a lone unit names nothing Node would have found (decisions.md "frame-lone-surrogate")
a phone's machine-written account of a reconnect (phase, state and issue tokens); the core keeps only [A-Za-z0-9_=@:. -] of it for its log
a provider's raw model record, kept as given
a provider's raw usage object (counts and provider keys), kept as given
a provider's raw usage object, kept as given
a pull-request number

a record's key, not a label: the core finds the record by it or checks it is unique by it (a schedule, webhook, MCP server, plugin, built-in tool or feature, skill, environment variable), as Node did by the same string; the label a person reads is a separate field where one exists

a secret, token or credential name: compared by the service that issued it, never shown; a pasted secret holding a lone unit is not the secret (Node sent the escape as given, UTF-8 conversion makes it U+FFFD), so the request is refused with the field named rather than sending a different secret
a selector of files (glob or path), compared with file names
a setting value at any path, of any shape: the relay-writable paths (RELAY_SETTING_PATHS, service.rs) hold booleans and enums, the others ids and scopes; no setting the clients write is typed text
a sign-in address or a secret sent to a service as it is: compared by that service, never shown as text
a time, date, duration, version or schedule field, parsed into a number or matched against a fixed form
a tool, model, provider or parameter id that the core matches against its catalog or tool list; the text a person reads beside it (displayName, description, label) is listed as free text
an effort level or output style id from a fixed list
an executable path run as a process: a path, not text
an id, cursor, revision or digest the core, a client or a service generated: matched against its record, never typed text
an image's bytes (base64) and the metadata line the resize wrote from it, not typed text
as config/value/write /value
compared with the file's content on disk (the stale-content check): a lone unit there equalled nothing in Node; read as U+FFFD it would equal a real U+FFFD, so it is refused
encoded bytes or a media type (base64, data URL, SDP), decoded, not text
host-only (an agent queue entry's context): a connection's request carrying it is invalidParams before any check of its text
provider-owned continuation state (cache names, response ids, account ids) that the providers compare with their own; it never holds typed text
provider-owned continuation state, as modelProxy/run /call/request/options/providerState
the client app's own name, a constant of the shipped client

an MCP server's header value, sent on every request to the server: Node saves the config and its fetch refuses the value when it connects (`Cannot convert argument to a ByteString`), sending nothing; the core's HTTP library would send the U+FFFD bytes, so the request is refused before anything is saved (recorded: native/core/fixtures/lone-surrogate-wire mcp-add-header-lone, mcp-save-header-lone)

Language-server params a person reads or a document receives as given: an item's detail, documentation, label details and tooltips, a code action's title and disabled reason, a command's title, a call-hierarchy item's detail, a signature's label and documentation, and the new text of an edit (insert text, text edits, workspace-edit text and change annotations). The server shows them or writes them into a document and compares them with nothing; Node sent a lone unit there as its JSON escape and the core sends U+FFFD, the replacement glyph either way (decisions.md "frame-lone-surrogate").

a language-server lookup key or command: a rename's new name (the identifier written into the code), a workspace-symbol query (matched against the server's symbols), a command (run by the server), a trigger or typed character, a completion item's label, sort and filter text, commit characters, a signature parameter's label (a range of its signature's label) and a call-hierarchy item's name. Node forwards a lone unit as its JSON escape to the server, which looks it up or runs it; read as U+FFFD it would name something else, so the request is refused (recorded: native/core/fixtures/lone-surrogate-wire lsp-rename-lone, lsp-workspace-symbol-lone, lsp-execute-command-lone)

a language-server URI, token, result id or annotation id (a document, a work-done or partial-result token, a semantic-tokens result, a workspace edit's document or annotation keys): an address the server resolves, never typed text

a diagnostic the server published, sent back in a code action request (its code, source, message, related information and description link): the server matches it with its own diagnostics, so text that differs matches none

a language-server word from a fixed vocabulary (a markup kind, a code action kind or `only` filter, a resource operation kind) or a formatting option's name and value: matched by the server, never typed text
language-server data the server wrote or runs, sent back whole (an item's or diagnostic's `data`, a command's arguments): opaque to the client, looked up or executed by the server
